summary: Defines a portion of the Management Information Base for managing expressions of MIB objects, so values can be calculated from others.

eli5.summary: This lets a device compute new numbers from existing ones, like adding up counters.

questions: how do snmp mib expressions work
what is delta sampling in snmp
how to compute custom mib objects
subtitle: Lets a device compute new MIB values from existing ones with C-style expressions, ready to feed into events.

tldr.problem: Managers often want MIB objects that the MIB designers never provided, and needs vary too much to keep adding standard objects.
tldr.mechanism: The Expression MIB lets a manager define an expression over existing MIB objects, using a subset of ANSI C syntax, with absolute, delta or changed sampling and optional wildcards. The results appear as ordinary MIB objects.
tldr.outcome: The computed values can be read like any other object or used by the Event MIB as trigger tests. It is a Proposed Standard and the text records no replacement.

today: RFC 2982 is a Proposed Standard, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It is the companion to the Event MIB in RFC 2981.

sections.title: The Idea of Custom MIB Objects
sections.content:
Users of MIBs often want objects that MIB designers have not provided, and the need varies from one management philosophy to another. Rather than fill more MIBs with standardized objects, RFC 2982 supports externally defined expressions of existing MIB objects.

The result of an evaluated expression is a MIB object that can be used like any other. A management application can read it directly, another MIB such as the Event MIB (RFC 2981) can reference it, and the Expression MIB can even use it in expressions of expressions.

The RFC says the MIB is meant for a relatively powerful, resource-rich managed system, though it can be stripped down for smaller ones. A typical use is custom objects for the Event MIB: a complex expression can evaluate to a rate of flow or a boolean and then be tested as an event trigger.
sections.eli5: Instead of waiting for someone to build every gauge you might want, you build your own gauge from the ones that already exist.

sections.title: How the MIB Is Structured
sections.content:
The MIB has three sections: Resource, Definition and Value.

  • Resource objects manage how much CPU and memory wildcarded delta expressions can use.
  • The Definition section has an expression table, indexed by expression owner and name, holding the expression text, the result data type and the sampling interval. An object table, indexed by owner, name and object index, describes each object in the expression: its object identifier, sample type, discontinuity indicator and so on.
  • The Value section has a value table with the evaluated results. It acts as a discriminated union: for a given expression only the column matching its result type is instantiated.

Results are identified by the column object (such as expValueCounter32Val), the expression owner, the expression name and an OID fragment. The fragment begins with 0.0, followed by another 0 when there is no wildcarding, or the instance that satisfied the wildcard.
sections.eli5: There is a recipe card (the formula), a list of ingredients (the objects it uses), and a results shelf where the finished answers are placed.

sections.title: Expression Syntax
sections.content:
An expression is an octet string of 1 to 1024 characters. Apart from the variable names it is in ANSI C syntax, restricted to a subset of operators and functions. Variables are written as a dollar sign and an integer matching an object index, for example ($1-$5)*100. Expressions must not be recursive, and the managed system must check for that.

Allowed operators cover parentheses, unary minus, arithmetic (+ - * / %), bitwise (& | ^ << >> ~) and logical or comparison operators. Conditionals produce an unsigned 32-bit value of 0 for false or 1 for true. The defined functions are counter32, counter64, arraySection, stringBegins, stringEnds, stringContains, oidBegins, oidEnds, oidContains, average, maximum, minimum, sum and exists.

The result type is chosen with expExpressionValueType: counter32, unsigned32, timeTicks, integer32, ipAddress, octetString, objectId or counter64. If the result cannot be made into that type, an invalidOperandType error occurs.
sections.eli5: The formulas look like the math you would write in a simple programming language, with a short list of allowed symbols and helper tools.

sections.title: Sampling, Wildcards and Evaluation
sections.content:
Each object in an expression is sampled one of three ways: absoluteValue (its present value), deltaValue (the present value minus the value sampled one delta interval ago) or changedValue (a boolean for whether the value differs from the previous sample). Counters are meaningless as absolute values, so they need delta sampling. Delta sampling requires keeping state and sampling continuously whether or not anyone is looking, which creates constant overhead.

Wildcards let one expression apply to many instances of the same object. The definer gives a partial object identifier, and the system uses the equivalent of GetNext to discover instances. All wildcarded objects in an expression must have the same semantics for the missing portion, and the expression is evaluated only for instances where every object is available with the same wildcarded value.

Timing depends on the sampling. With no delta or changed values, evaluation happens on demand, so every requester gets a freshly calculated value. With delta or changed values, evaluation runs every sample period and requesters see the value as of the last period. If an evaluation fails in one period, the value from the previous successful period must not be carried forward.
sections.eli5: For counters like an odometer, the useful number is how far you drove since last time, so the machine remembers the last reading. With wildcards, one formula is reused for every similar item, like every network port.

sections.title: Worked Examples
sections.content:
The RFC gives two examples. The first uses a deliberately far-fetched pair of tables to compute a percentage across a wildcard: the expression 100*$1/$2 divides blessings in one town (hardwired to town 976) by total blessings per person, with the person index wildcarded. For people numbered 6, 19 and 42, the value instances are 0.0.6, 0.0.19 and 0.0.42.

The second computes line utilization of a half-duplex link, adapted from a book cited in the RFC: (ifInOctets + ifOutOctets) * 800 / seconds / ifSpeed. The octet counters are delta sampled, the delta interval is 6 seconds, and a conditional expression restricts the result to interfaces that directly represent actual hardware. The result could then serve as an event threshold, per RFC 2981, to watch for overutilization of hardware connections.
sections.eli5: One example works out what share of a total belongs to one town. The other turns bytes counted on a network cable into how busy the cable is, as a percentage.

sections.title: Errors and Resource Limits
sections.content:
When evaluation fails, the error table records the time, the character index in the expression, an error code and the instance being evaluated. There are 11 error codes, including invalidSyntax, undefinedObjectIndex, unrecognizedOperator, unrecognizedFunction, invalidOperandType, unmatchedParenthesis, tooManyWildcardValues, recursion, deltaTooShort, resourceUnavailable and divideByZero. Errors found when setting the expression fail the Set with wrongValue, while errors during a Get return genErr, except two that return resourceUnavailable.

To limit cost, the delta interval is 0 to 86400 seconds, and resource objects set a minimum delta interval and a maximum number of wildcard delta instances. The RFC also describes lighter subsets: leaving out wildcards, or leaving out deltas, which would make expressions on counters unusable.
sections.eli5: If the formula is broken or the machine runs out of room, it writes down what went wrong and where, so a person can fix it.

sections.title: Security
sections.content:
The RFC looks at two concerns: protecting expressions from tampering or unauthorized use of resources, and protecting the objects used in the calculation. Access to expressions follows the expression owner and view-based access control (RFC 2575). Objects inside an expression are read using the security credentials recorded when the creator made the expression active.

One consequence is called out: the results of an expression could be made available to someone who does not have access to the raw data behind them. Depending on the situation and security policy, that could be legitimate or a violation.
sections.eli5: The formula can only use numbers its author was allowed to see. But the answer might be shared with people who cannot see those numbers, which can be fine or a problem.

items.title: absoluteValue
items.text: The present value of the object. This is the default.

items.title: deltaValue
items.text: The present value minus the previous value, sampled one delta interval ago. Meant mainly for counters.

items.title: changedValue
items.text: 1 if the value differs from the previous sample, 0 if not.
